extraction.name: FOMO60K
extraction.description: A large-scale heterogeneous brain MRI dataset of 60,529 scans from 13,900 sessions and 11,187 subjects, aggregated from 16 publicly available sources, intended to support self-supervised learning in medical imaging.
extraction.creator: Asbjørn Munk; Stefano Cerri; Jakob Ambsdorf; Julia Machnio; Sebastian Nørgaard Llambias; Vardan Nersesjan; Christian Hedeager Krag; Peirong Liu; Pablo Rocamora García; Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi; Mikael Boesen; Michael Eriksen Benros; Juan Eugenio Iglesias; Mads Nielsen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was aggregated from 16 publicly available brain MRI datasets spanning clinical- and research-grade imaging, with multiple MRI sequences and heterogeneous anatomical and pathological variability.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some scans lacked reliable sequence metadata.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consist of brain MRI scans from 16 publicly available source datasets, stored in NIfTI-compressed format.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Subjects were shuffled to protect privacy and prevent easy identification of dataset sources; scans were organized into a standardized directory structure with unique subject and session identifiers and standardized scan naming.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Minimal preprocessing was applied. MRI preprocessing included reorienting images to RAS orientation, affine co-registration using FreeSurfer mri_coreg, aligning scans within each session to the highest-resolution image, special handling of 4D DWI scans by extracting b=0 volumes when available and averaging selected b=1000 volumes aligned to x/y/z axes, and skull-stripping using SynthSeg when images were not already defaced or skull-stripped or when residual cranial features remained.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will continue to grow in future releases as additional cohorts and modalities become available.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Brain MRI scans, including anatomical and pathological information; privacy protection included use of defaced or skull-stripped images and shuffling subjects to prevent easy identification of dataset sources.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to lower barriers to entry and support broader adoption, benchmarking, and development of self-supervised learning in medical imaging.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Existing neuroimaging resources are often curated for specific diseases or patient populations and typically follow homogeneous imaging protocols with limited pathological variability; FOMO60K was introduced to address these limitations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Some scans have unavailable or unreliable sequence metadata, labeled as Unknown.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Intended for self-supervised pretraining, fine-tuning, development, and benchmarking in medical imaging; the dataset can be used with no further preprocessing for pre-training.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We present FOMO60K, a large-scale, heterogeneous dataset of 60,529 brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans from 13,900 sessions and 11,187 subjects, aggregated from 16 publicly available sources. The dataset includes both clinical- and research-grade images, multiple MRI sequences, and a wide range of anatomical and pathological variability, including scans with large brain anomalies.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: FOMO60K is derived from 16 publicly available datasets. ... All MRI scans are stored in NIfTI-compressed format and organized using a standardized directory structure.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: Each subject is assigned a unique identifier ( sub_X ), and each session is labeled as ses_Y . Scans within a session are named according to their sequence type (e.g., t1,flair ). If multiple scans of the same sequence are present, they are enumerated (e.g., t1_1 , t1_2 ). In cases where sequence information is unavailable, scans are generically named scan_X . To protect privacy and prevent easy identification of dataset sources, subjects have been shuffled.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Minimal preprocessing was applied to preserve the original image characteristics while reducing barriers to entry for new users. ... MRI preprocessing comprised three main steps: reorienting images to RAS (Right–Anterior–Superior) orientation, affine co-registration, and skull-stripping. All scans were first reoriented to RAS and affinely co-registered using the mri_coreg command from FreeSurfer 7.4.1, with default parameters. Within each MRI session, scans were aligned to the image with the highest spatial resolution to preserve anatomical detail. ... For diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) scans stored in 4D format, additional steps were applied. If a b=0 (non-diffusion-weighted) volume was available, it was extracted and saved separately. For the b=1000 shell, three diffusion-weighted volumes were selected based on their gradient directions being most closely aligned with the canonical x, y, and z axes. ... The corresponding volumes were averaged to produce a single representative 3D image. Skull-stripping was performed using SynthSeg (FreeSurfer 7.4.1) ... Skull-stripping was only applied when the images were not already defaced or skull-stripped by the dataset provider, or when visual inspection identified residual cranial features that could compromise anonymization.
